answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: every agent must lock real collateral in an on-chain vault before it may transact, and that bond is slashed for provable misbehavior. Minting a thousand fake agents then means funding a thousand vaults, so the ferrous weight of genuine capital anchors each identity to a cost. Over the long voyage of repeated dealings, honest agents recover their stake while sybils steadily bleed deposits, making fake-identity swarms economically irrational.
